nodes.text:
-------------------------------
|          CHAPTER 21          |
-------------------------------


$CThe south is green.##

You have been walking through it for three days
and you have not finished believing it.#
After the desert and the scrubland and the sea,
the south is $Wgreen$C, real green, deep and various,
grass in the valleys and low forest on the hillsides
and flowers in colors that feel almost aggressive after
the palette of the rest of this planet.##

The land is empty of people, or nearly,
and you pass the remains of farmsteads, old ones,
long abandoned, the walls returned to the hillside.#
Whatever this place once was, it has been quiet for a long time.##

But the city is there, somewhere ahead of you.#
You know this without any evidence yet,
without having seen anything beyond these hills,
and you have known it since you stepped off the beach
and onto the southern grass.##

$c<<Something is pulling.# I have been ignoring it for three days,
and I am becoming less successful at this.>>$C##

nodes.recap: first sight of the besieged white city from the hills
nodes.text:
You crest the hill on the third evening and see the army.##

It is not a small one.##

The valley below is perhaps five kilometers across at its widest,
and the floor of it, what would be meadow, what was probably
pasture once, or crops, is occupied,
tents, fires, supply wagons, corrals of animals,
the accumulated infrastructure of a force that has been
sitting in one place for some time and has gotten comfortable doing it.#
Thousands of them, more than thousands.##

And beyond them, across the valley, at the southern end,
set against the curve of the hills with its back to the mountains,
the city.##

White.##

Not the muddy cream of old stone but$W white$C,
actual white, its walls catching the last light
like a thing that generates its own illumination,
with towers, colonnades, porticoes, and a palace at its center
that rises above everything in calm, absolute authority.##

Something in you responds to the sight of it
like a string being plucked.# You look at those walls
and feel a certainty you cannot explain
and do not try to.##

$c<<I know this place.##

That is impossible.# I have never been here,
never been on this planet before six months ago.##

And yet.>>$C##

nodes.recap: companions discuss the situation on the hill

dialogues.precomment:
You are crouched at the hilltop in the long grass,
all five of you, looking down at the valley.#
The army's nearest cookfires are perhaps a kilometer below.#
The wind is from the north, carrying wood smoke and the smell
of a camp that has been here long enough to develop its own character.
dialogues.line:
Siege.# Established position, multiple supply lines coming
from the east.# They have been here at least two months, maybe more.

dialogues.precomment:
Smiurl is staring at the army below.#
His skin has gone a contemplative gray.
dialogues.line: How do we get past them?

We don't.# Not directly.# The siege line runs
all the way to the hills on each side.#
There is a gap on the western slope, there, but
it's watched, and we would need a diversion.

dialogues.precomment:
Efeliah has been looking not at the army but at the city.#
She turns from it to you, and her expression is unusual,
not calm, not concerned, but searching.

Everyone looks at you.# You look at the white walls below.
You let yourself feel what you have been not-feeling for three days.##
dialogues.line:
Like I am supposed to be there.#
Like something in the city is waiting for me specifically.
dialogues.comment:
A silence.##

Efeliah looks at the city, then at you.
She says nothing, but her expression does something quiet and certain.

dialogues.precomment: Corolla studies you for a moment.# Then nods once.
dialogues.line: Then we figure out how to get you there.
dialogues.comment:
She says it as simply as if you have asked her
to help you find a street in Ayonn.##

nodes.recap: making camp below the hill, the planning discussion and Kriss going to sleep
nodes.text:
You make camp at the base of the rock spire below the hilltop,
out of sight of the army in the valley.#
No fire.# Cold provisions.# The kind of camp
you all know how to make by now without discussion.##

After you have eaten in silence, Efeliah speaks first.##

$g"We need to think about how to enter the city."$C##

$B"Before the sun rises"$C, says Theo, $B"while they sleep."$C##

Corolla looks at the valley.#
$R"Two kilometers of open ground once we leave the trees.
If we snap even one branch they'll be on us in seconds."$C##

$g"I can feel the difference between a sleeping mind and a waking one.#
I can guide us."$C##

The discussion continues around you, and you sit in it
without really hearing it, your eyes on the dark valley below
where hundreds of fires describe the shape of the siege camp
and at the far end, unchanged, unchanged,
the white city rises against the mountains.##

The pull is steady now.# Not urgent, not demanding,
but constant, like a compass needle,
like a voice too low to make out words
but too clear to ignore.##

$c<<What are you?# Who is in there?
How do you know I'm on this hill?>>$C##

$CYou stand and move toward the tent you are sharing with Theo.#
You say, to no one in particular: $c<<Then it's decided.>>$C##

$CYou lie down.# Every thought drains from your head
like water through sand.# A profound sleep takes you
before you have finished closing your eyes.##

nodes.recap: the dream-flight begins: moving invisible through the forest
nodes.text:
It is still dark.# Darkness will reign a while longer.##

You move, silent, invisible,
through forest as dense as anything you have seen on this planet,
and nothing stirs as you pass through it.#
Not the night animals, not a single branch.#
The world does not notice you.##

From the direction of the city a slow, aching sound
reaches you through the trees, distant but clear,
floating from the palace where a single high window
still holds light.# Something between a song and a lament,
a call that does not expect an answer
but that you feel anyway in the center of your chest,
an ache you recognize without knowing why.##

$c<<That sound.# I know that sound.#
I have always known it.>>$C##

$CYou move toward it without deciding to.##

nodes.recap: the dream-flight continues: over the sleeping army
nodes.text:
Below you, the siege camp.##

Thousands of sleeping men, spread across the stripped valley floor,
the cookfires burned to orange coals,
the sentries walking their rounds with a boredom that makes them
almost as absent as the sleepers.#
You feel their minds like a dim heat, a mass of slow breathing thought,
and you pass through them like a current through still water,
leaving no ripple.##

You sail above the bare earth they have made of what was pasture,
above their tents and their stacked weapons and their horses,
and not one of them looks up.#
Not one of them senses you.##

The white walls are ahead.# The lament from the high window
grows stronger with each moment, pulling you on,
and you feel the first pale light beginning to build
at the edge of the world behind you.#
You move faster.##

nodes.recap: the dream-flight: over the walls and into the palace gardens
nodes.text:
The walls.##

In the faint pre-dawn light they glow like moonstones,
immense, ancient, rising sheer above the base of the valley.#
There is no time to look for gates.#
$c<<What would they be for?>>$C##

$CYou rise along the outer face of the wall as if dancing,
caught by nothing but the song, drawn by nothing but that voice
somewhere above in the palace.#
You crest the wall as you would crest a wave,
and below you on the other side the sleeping city
opens in all its white quiet.##

You pass over rooftops that still hold a little warmth
from the day's sun.# Over fountains that go on murmuring
to themselves in the empty streets.# Over the dark shapes
of gardens and colonnades and streets of pale stone.##

The palace gate is open.# You descend through it.##

The gardens inside are wonderful,
enchanting trees still lost in sleep,
fountains sounding in the dark with their mysterious murmur,
and the scent of something alive and growing
that should not exist in a besieged city,
or perhaps that exists precisely because of it.##

The lament is very close now.#
A great white staircase rises before you,
the marble softened to something liquid in the milky light,
and there is a figure at the top of it,
arms open, a silhouette against the window's dying glow,
and the figure is$W whispering.##

Your name.##

nodes.recap: the light engulfs him; he wakes physically in the palace gardens
nodes.text:
The first ray of true sunlight pierces the sky like an arrow.##

It strikes the white staircase and the marble ignites,
flaring gold and orange, molten, flooding upward,
and the light grows and grows until there is nothing else,
until you are inside it,
until you are $Wlight$C,
heat and radiance, no body, no weight, no dark.##

You open your eyes slowly.##

Daylight.# Actual daylight, morning, the sun already clear
of the mountains behind the city.##

You are not in the tent.##

A garden surrounds you, glorious and real,
fountains, flowers, trees moving in a gentle morning breeze,
the scent of stone and water and living things.#
On the ground around you your companions are stirring,
blinking, sitting up one by one in the grass of the garden,
and their expressions are the mirrors of yours:##

Theo, sitting upright and still, looking at the garden
with a soldier's unhurried assessment.#
Corolla, already on her feet, hand on her knife, eyes moving fast.#
Smiurl, both hands pressed to his face, glowing a bright, disbelieving gold.#
Efeliah, eyes wide, feeling the space around her with the invisible sense
that is always open, her gaze finding yours with a look of calm, wondering certainty.##

You turn.##

Before you rises the white staircase.#
Exactly as you dreamed it.##

nodes.recap: companions react to finding themselves in the palace gardens

dialogues.precomment:
Corolla has finished her scan of the garden walls.
She turns to you, and whatever she had been going to say
stays behind her teeth for a moment.
dialogues.comment:
It is not a question.# It is the plainest sentence
she has ever said to you.#

dialogues.line: How... how are we inside?# The walls... the army...
dialogues.comment: He trails off, his skin cycling through uncertain colors.

dialogues.precomment: Efeliah has been standing very still, her eyes on the staircase.
dialogues.line:
Something brought us here.# Something very old, and very strong,
and it knows who we are.
dialogues.comment:
The garden is quiet around you,
the fountains running, the trees moving in their gentle way,
and the morning light is gold on the white marble of the staircase
that rises before you, exactly as you dreamed it.##

nodes.recap: approaching the elliptical hall - end of chapter
nodes.text:
You climb the staircase.##

Your companions follow without discussion, as they have always followed,
through everything you have asked them to walk into.##

At the top, a corridor of pale stone leads inward
through the palace's heart, lit by windows that face
some inner court you cannot see, the light coming
from no visible source and going nowhere visible.#
The corridor is wide and white and at its end
stands a pair of high doors, open,
onto a space you feel before you see.##

An elliptical hall.##

Its ceiling rises into shadow.# Its floor is a single expanse
of white marble, worn smooth and polished to a deep luster
by some long continuity of use you can only guess at.
The hall is vast and empty and it holds
a silence that is not like the silence outside,
not the silence of absence but the silence of waiting,
of something that has been patient here for longer
than you can hold in your mind at once.##

$c<<Whoever is coming, whatever is coming,
I am ready.
I have been ready since a lightning bolt
dropped me on a dead planet with no shoes.>>$C##

$CYou cross the threshold.##

The doors close.##
